content:
Today we continue the same beautiful subject of the manna. We have already seen that Yahweh fed Israel in the wilderness with bread from heaven. It came down with the dew, it was small like seed, white and pure, sweet like honey, and rich like cakes prepared with fresh oil. Today we look at another deep part of this picture; the manna that could not normally be stored, and what happened when the people tried to keep it against Yahweh's command.

Yahweh gave Israel a daily command concerning the manna. Moses said, "Do not keep any of it until morning" (Exodus 16:19). Now this was not merely a rule about food. It was a test of trust. Israel had to learn that Yahweh would provide again tomorrow. They were not to gather in fear, store in unbelief, and live as though Yahweh might somehow fail them the next day. Every morning they had to go out again and depend on Him again. Every morning their faith was quietly being trained.

This teaches us that Yahweh's Word must be gathered fresh every day. Christ taught us to pray, "Give us today the food we need" (Matthew 6:11). And when the tempter came to him, he answered that people do not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God (Matthew 4:4). Therefore yesterday's gathering cannot feed today's soul. Yesterday's lesson was good for yesterday's strength, but today has its own trials, its own temptations, its own duties, and its own needs. The Bereans give us a beautiful example of this. Acts 17:11 says they received the Word eagerly and searched the Scriptures daily. They did not treat the Word of God as an occasional duty to be done now and then. They searched daily. This is the true gathering of manna; daily study, daily prayer, daily meditation, and daily communion with Yahweh.

But some of the Israelites did not listen. Exodus 16:20 says they kept some of the manna until morning, and it was full of maggots and had a terrible smell. Think of that carefully. What was sweet yesterday became corrupt when it was kept against Yahweh's command. The very same food that had nourished them the day before now bred worms and gave off a stench. And here lies a very serious lesson for us. If we rest only upon what we learned yesterday and gather nothing fresh today, even what we already had may begin to lose its power in our life. Truth that is not renewed, obeyed, and used can quietly fade from the heart. Christ said, "To those who use well what they are given, even more will be given, but from those who do nothing, even what little they have will be taken away" (Matthew 25:29).

This shows us that a stagnant believer does not simply remain where he is. Slowly, quietly, he begins to move backward. Hebrews 2:1 warns us to listen very carefully to the truth we have heard, or we may drift away from it. And drifting does not usually happen in one dramatic moment. It happens quietly, when the daily gathering stops. Prayer becomes weak. Study becomes rare. Meditation becomes dry. And then, little by little, the heart begins to lose the freshness of the manna. No one plans to drift. It simply happens to those who stop gathering.

The manna that was wrongly stored also developed a bad smell, and this shows us another danger. Truth held in disobedience, truth used for pride, or truth twisted into wrong doctrine becomes a stench before Yahweh. The Word of God is pure, sweet, and life-giving when it is handled correctly. But when men mishandle it, twist it, or use it to support error, what was given as bread can become corruption. Paul warned about those who had strayed from the truth and said that such teaching spreads like a disease (2 Timothy 2:17-18). He also showed that our service should be a sweet fragrance of Christ before God (2 Corinthians 2:15), yet he said that to some the very same message becomes "an aroma of death" (2 Corinthians 2:16, NLT). The Word of Yahweh is never the problem. The danger lies in how men receive it, store it, handle it, and use it.

So the ordinary manna could not be kept. It had to be gathered fresh, eaten that day, and gathered again the next morning. That was the rule for all the manna that fell in the wilderness. But there was one exception; one single portion that Yahweh commanded to be kept, and that portion never spoiled at all. It was placed in a golden jar and set before Yahweh Himself, and it remained fresh through all the generations. Why did that one portion never decay when every other portion bred worms? And what is Yahweh showing us in that preserved omer of bread? That is where we will continue tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

Keep us from the quiet drift that begins when the daily gathering stops.

We do not want to live on yesterday's manna while today's heart grows dry.

Give us fresh bread every morning, and teach us to trust You for tomorrow's portion.

Guard us from handling Your truth with pride or disobedience, lest sweetness turn to corruption.

Make us like the Bereans, searching Your Word eagerly and daily.

Come, let us press on to know Yahweh. He will respond to us as surely as the arrival of dawn. - Hosea 6:3, NLT

In the name of Christ, the true bread from heaven, we pray. Amen.
